solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pamper priest passing over English border

indicators.note: the priest's title stretches over the letter for English, straddling and so enclosing it

parts.note: a Catholic priest is addressed as Father
a border in a garden is a flower bed

explanation.surface: A cleric skirting England's frontier is somehow being spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' looks like the frontier of England, but in gardening a border is a bed of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: To featherbed someone is an idiom for cosseting or spoiling them with every comfort.

clue.text: Choose artist to portray Agamemnon's daughter

parts.note: to elect is to choose, as at the ballot box
RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword stock artist

explanation.surface: A director picks an artist to paint a heroine of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the child of King Agamemnon who avenges his murder with her brother Orestes.

clue.text: A number seem oddly on edge

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters of the word seem, the first and third

explanation.surface: Some figure appears strangely nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense is the same as being nervous and keyed up, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Former players, demanding types

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
actors are players on stage

explanation.surface: Retired performers can be difficult and insistent people.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word, the pieces make a noun for people who exact payment or obedience.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who exacts, that is insists on or extorts, so exactors are people who demand things.

clue.text: Explosive beauty, like Marilyn Monroe?

parts.note: a stunning fair-haired woman is called by a phrase whose second word is literally an explosive shell, and Monroe was the classic example

explanation.surface: A description of a dazzling film star such as Marilyn Monroe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a very attractive fair-haired woman, a label Monroe made famous in Hollywood.

clue.text: State of senile decay demonstrated by magistrate imprisoning volunteers

indicators.note: the magistrate's word locks the volunteers' letters inside it

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A judge jailing volunteers shows his mental decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the weakened mental state of old age, when someone dotes or becomes feeble-minded.

clue.text: Miss sleep after onset of storm

indicators.note: the nap word follows the letter from storm
the start of the word storm, its opening letter only

parts.note: kip is British slang for a sleep

explanation.surface: Losing sleep once a storm begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to miss it out or leave it out, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Result of match has cronies going wild about the Spanish

indicators.note: the scrambled cronies go round the Spanish article
the letters of cronies run riot into a new order

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: After the match, the result sends a group of pals into wild celebration about the Spaniards.
explanation.walkthrough: The cronies look like football fans celebrating, but they are anagram fodder; the Spanish article sits within the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreline is the final score of a game as printed, such as two-one.

clue.text: Trendy? That girl has to be with it to take over

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
her refers to a girl just mentioned

explanation.surface: A fashionable young woman must be cool to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to take over property or a role from a predecessor, a sense of succession.

clue.text: Soldiers circling a base

indicators.note: the soldiers surround the letter a on both sides

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops surround a military camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military base, but it is the adjective meaning low or ignoble.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and mean are both adjectives for low, contemptible or ungenerous behaviour.

clue.text: Punctuation mark, perhaps too misused

indicators.note: the letters of perhaps too are wrongly used, so reordered

explanation.surface: A grammar pedant's complaint that a punctuation mark is often misused.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is the raised comma marking possession or omitted letters, one of the punctuation marks.

clue.text: A B in examination, taking the most optimistic view

indicators.note: the grade letter is put inside the exam word

parts.note: a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Scoring a B in an exam is the best one can hope for.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means 'even under the most favourable interpretation', as in 'at best it was a draw'.

clue.text: Foolish constable found in nasty bog in part of Ulster

indicators.note: the jumbled marsh word is located within the Northern Irish place name

parts.note: Derry is a city and county in Northern Ireland, part of the province of Ulster

indicators.note: a nasty mess of the letters of bog, reworked

explanation.surface: A dim policeman is discovered in a filthy bog in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogberry is the Shakespeare character; the bog here is a muddle of letters, not a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogberry is the bumbling malapropising constable in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.

clue.text: Crustacean in catch caught by seaman crossing river

parts.note: to land a fish is to catch it

indicators.note: the river's letter goes across the middle of caught-plus-sailor, inside them

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor crossing a river catches something in his net.
explanation.definitionFit: A land crab is a crab species that lives mainly on land, a type of crustacean.

clue.text: Overalls with muck on are, and sleeveless vest

parts.note: dung is muck or manure

indicators.note: the outer letters of vest are cut off like sleeves, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: Work clothes covered in filth, worn with a sleeveless vest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are trousers with a bib and straps, a kind of overalls worn for manual work.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about batting against spinner? No end

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in

indicators.note: the toy's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricket question: is someone keen on batting facing a spin bowler for ever?
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler, but it is the toy top, losing its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is an informal idiom for being keen on or absorbed by it.

clue.text: You're quite mistaken to overlook Italian

parts.note: to forget something is to overlook it
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: Telling someone they are wrong to ignore an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial brush-off meaning 'not at all, you are wrong', as in 'me apologise? Not a chance'.

clue.text: Run out from square leg

indicators.note: the opening letter comes out from the word square

parts.note: pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A batsman runs out his partner from the square-leg position in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUARE LEG is a fielding position in cricket; here 'leg' is PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a short pleasure trip in a car, a run out for fun.

clue.text: Criticise expert before a remedy for all is produced

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A critic slams an expert just before a cure-all appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed universal cure, a medicine that fixes every ill.

clue.text: Lecture on the American elk in a Canadian city

indicators.note: in an across clue the talking-to comes after, on top of, the animal

parts.note: Americans call the large deer that Europeans name elk a moose
to jaw is to lecture or harangue

explanation.surface: A talk about North American wildlife given in a Canadian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Moose Jaw is a city in Saskatchewan, on the Canadian prairies.

clue.text: Reportedly, a sailor can be offensive

indicators.note: as reported in speech, the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; an old salt is a sailor, so a sailor is a salt

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that a seaman can be rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective meaning rude, but it is the noun: a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is an attack, and so is an assault, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Carried round large island

parts.note: borne is the past participle of bear, carry
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone transported around a big island.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is the third largest island in the world, shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.

clue.text: Notorious home recognised by many

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a famous person is widely recognised

explanation.surface: A house known to the public for its bad reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamous means well known for something bad, the same as notorious.

clue.text: Game bird and beef

definitions.meaning: a plump moorland bird shot for sport
beef as slang verb means to grumble or complain

explanation.surface: A menu offering game and red meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a moorland bird hunted for sport and a verb meaning to moan or gripe.

clue.text: Discipline in class

definitions.meaning: keeping control and good behaviour, as in law and discipline
a rank in biological classification, between class and family

explanation.surface: A teacher keeping control in the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both obedience to rules and a taxonomic group ranking below a class.

clue.text: Cover international actor's trial

parts.note: a screen covers or hides something
a Test match is a cricket international between countries

explanation.surface: Hiding an international performer's court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen test is a filmed audition in which an actor is tried out for a part.

clue.text: Departs with strange revolving cylinder

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A weird spinning tube sets off.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum is a cylinder that turns, like the drum of a washing machine or a winch.

clue.text: Fish, black when small

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
as means when, as in 'as he left'
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A fish that is dark when it is young.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass is a spiny-finned sea fish, prized by anglers.

clue.text: Destroy old book, well-read

parts.note: a literate person is educated and well-read

explanation.surface: Ruining an old book that a scholar knows well.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out completely, a strong synonym for destroy.
